modules.title: North Pit Traffic Rules
modules.summary: Load, haul, dump, return — the loop that moves every tonne.
modules.practiceNote: Send one truck around the full cycle and watch each stage.

cards.title: Four stages, one loop
cards.body: Every truck repeats the same loop: it is LOADED by the excavator, HAULS the material along the road, DUMPS it at the dump point, then RETURNS empty for the next load.

cards.title: Cycle time
cards.body: Cycle time is how long one full loop takes. Shorter cycles mean more trips per shift. Waiting, detours and slow roads all make the cycle longer.
cards.keyPoint: More trips per shift = more tonnes moved.

cards.title: Payload
cards.body: Payload is the weight a truck carries on one trip. Production is simply payload × trips. A full, correctly loaded truck on a short cycle is the goal.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the haul cycle?

options.text: Haul → Load → Return → Dump
Load → Haul → Dump → Return
Dump → Load → Haul → Return

questions.explanation: A truck is loaded at the face, hauls to the dump point, dumps, then returns empty.

options.text: The time to load one bucket
The length of the whole shift
The time for one complete load-haul-dump-return loop

questions.explanation: Cycle time covers the full loop, including any waiting along the way.

questions.prompt: Which change moves more tonnes in the same shift?

options.text: Shortening the cycle time
Adding a longer detour
Sending trucks half full

questions.explanation: Production = payload × trips. A shorter cycle gives more trips.

modules.title: Bucket Passes & Truck Matching
modules.summary: Match truck size to the excavator so every load is full and fast.
modules.practiceNote: Two trucks of different sizes share one excavator — compare their loading.

cards.title: What is a bucket pass?
cards.body: Each scoop the excavator drops into a truck is one pass. A truck needs several passes to fill. Fewer, fuller passes load a truck faster.
cards.keyPoint: Passes to fill = truck payload ÷ bucket size.

cards.title: Match trucks to the loader
cards.body: A good match fills the truck in a whole number of passes (for example 4). A poor match leaves a last half-empty pass, or a truck so small the excavator waits between trucks.

cards.title: Never overload
cards.body: Loading past the rated payload strains tyres, brakes and the road, and can spill material. Stop at the rated payload, even if there is room.
cards.keyPoint: Full is good. Overloaded is unsafe.

questions.prompt: A truck carries 60 t and the bucket holds 15 t. How many passes to fill it?

options.text: 3 passes
4 passes
6 passes

questions.prompt: There is still space in the tray, but the truck has reached its rated payload. What should happen?

options.text: Add one more pass to use the space
Stop loading and send the truck

questions.explanation: Rated payload is the limit. Overloading is a safety and equipment risk.

modules.title: Queues & Idle Time
modules.summary: Waiting trucks cost time and fuel. Spread the fleet to keep it moving.
modules.practiceNote: Two excavators, two trucks — split them so nobody waits in line.

cards.title: Queues form at the loader
cards.body: An excavator can only load one truck at a time. If trucks arrive faster than it can load them, the others wait in a queue.

cards.title: Idle time is lost time
cards.body: A truck waiting in line burns fuel and moves nothing. Utilization — the share of time a machine is working — drops.
cards.keyPoint: Watch the queue time. High queue = too many trucks on one loader.

cards.title: Balance the fleet
cards.body: When one loader has a queue and another is waiting for trucks, move a truck across. The best plan keeps both excavators and trucks busy.

questions.prompt: Three trucks are queuing at Excavator A while Excavator B has none. What is the best move?

options.text: Reassign a truck to Excavator B
Add another truck to Excavator A
Do nothing — queues are normal

questions.explanation: Moving a truck to the idle loader cuts queue time and raises production.

questions.prompt: A truck waiting in a queue with its engine running is…

options.text: Productive time
Idle time that burns fuel

questions.explanation: Waiting moves no material but still uses fuel.

options.text: How fast a truck can drive
How much fuel a truck holds
The share of time equipment is actually working

questions.explanation: Higher utilization means less waiting and more work done.

modules.title: Route Choice & Traffic
modules.summary: The shortest road is not always the fastest. Plan around traffic.
modules.practiceNote: Try each route and compare the trip time.

cards.title: Short vs. fast
cards.body: A short road with a steep ramp, mud or heavy traffic can be slower than a longer, clear road. Choose the route with the best total trip time.
cards.keyPoint: Judge a route by time, not distance.

cards.title: Intersections and traffic
cards.body: Where haul roads cross, trucks must slow down and give way. Too many trucks on one road create jams. Spreading traffic keeps everyone moving.

questions.prompt: Route A is shorter but muddy and busy. Route B is longer but clear. Which is usually better?

options.text: Always Route A — it is shorter
The route with the shorter total trip time, often B

questions.explanation: Mud and traffic slow trucks down. Total time matters most.

questions.prompt: What causes traffic jams on haul roads?

options.text: Too many trucks sharing one road or crossing
Trucks that are fully loaded
Using more than one route

questions.explanation: Crowded roads and busy intersections force trucks to wait.

modules.title: Fuel Planning
modules.summary: Refuel on your terms, not when the tank runs dry on the ramp.
modules.practiceNote: Watch fuel levels and send trucks to the fuel bay before they run low.

cards.title: Every trip burns fuel
cards.body: Loaded trucks, uphill ramps and long idling burn the most fuel. A truck that runs out stops where it is and blocks the road.

cards.title: Plan refuels
cards.body: Send trucks to refuel when they are empty and near the fuel bay, and stagger them so the whole fleet does not stop at once.
cards.keyPoint: Refuel early, empty and one at a time.

questions.prompt: When is the best time to send a truck to refuel?

options.text: When it is empty, low on fuel and near the fuel bay
Only after the tank is completely empty
Send every truck at the same time

questions.explanation: Planned, staggered refuels keep production running.

options.text: An empty truck on flat road
A loaded truck climbing a ramp

questions.explanation: Weight and grade both increase fuel burn.

modules.title: Site Safety Basics
modules.summary: Right of way, speed, narrow roads, breakdowns and pre-start checks.
modules.practiceNote: A truck will break down — react calmly and reroute the others.

cards.title: Loaded trucks have right of way
cards.body: A loaded haul truck is very heavy and needs a long distance to stop. Light vehicles and empty trucks give way to loaded trucks, especially on ramps.
cards.keyPoint: When in doubt, give way to the loaded truck.

cards.title: Speed limits and narrow roads
cards.body: Obey posted speed limits — they reflect grade, visibility and road condition. On one-way or single-lane sections, follow the signs and wait for the road to clear before entering.

cards.title: Breakdowns: stop, secure, report
cards.body: If a truck breaks down, stop in a safe spot, apply the park brake, turn on hazard lights and radio it in. Other drivers slow down and follow instructions to pass or reroute.
cards.keyPoint: Never try to push past a broken-down truck without clearance.

cards.title: Pre-start checks
cards.body: Before every shift, walk around the machine: tyres, lights, horn, brakes, mirrors, leaks and fluid levels. Report any fault before operating.

questions.prompt: A loaded haul truck and a light vehicle meet on a ramp. Who gives way?

options.text: The loaded haul truck
The light vehicle

questions.explanation: Loaded trucks have right of way — they cannot stop quickly.

questions.prompt: Your truck breaks down on the haul road. What do you do first?

options.text: Stop safely, secure the truck, turn on hazards and radio it in
Walk to the workshop to get help
Keep driving slowly to the dump

questions.explanation: Stop, secure and report so others can manage traffic safely.

questions.prompt: When should pre-start checks be done?

options.text: Once a week
Only if something sounds wrong
Before operating, at the start of every shift

questions.explanation: Pre-start checks catch faults before they become incidents.

glossary.definition: One scoop of material that the excavator drops into a truck. A truck is usually filled in a few passes.
The total time for one full trip: load, haul, dump and return to the loading point.
The place where trucks unload, such as a crusher, stockpile or waste dump.
A road built for heavy trucks to carry material between the pit and the dump point.
A truck carrying material. It is heavy and slow to stop, so it gets right of way.
Rock or material that contains something valuable and is sent for processing.
Waste rock and soil on top of the ore that must be removed first and taken to a waste dump.
The weight of material a truck carries on one trip, measured in tonnes.
A walk-around inspection of a machine before the shift: tyres, lights, brakes, leaks, fluids and alarms.
How much material is moved over time, usually tonnes per hour.
Time a truck spends waiting in line to be loaded or to dump.
Time a machine is running but not doing useful work, such as waiting with nothing to load.
Stopping at the fuel bay to top up. Planned refuels avoid trucks running dry on the road.
The rule for who goes first. On haul roads, loaded trucks and emergency vehicles usually go first.
Positioning a truck in the right place next to the excavator so it can be loaded safely and quickly.
Pairing trucks with an excavator so full loads take a whole number of bucket passes.
The share of time equipment spends working instead of waiting. Higher is better.
A berm (pile of material) along the edge of a haul road that helps stop vehicles from leaving the road.

prestart.title: DT-07 · Day shift
prestart.brief: Standard hauler parked in the ready line. Inspect it before your shift.

items.label: Tyres & rims
items.observation: Tread even, no cuts, all wheel nuts and indicators aligned.
items.explanation: Check for cuts, bulges, low pressure and loose or missing wheel nuts on every wheel.

items.label: Fluid leaks
items.observation: Ground under the truck is dry. No oil or coolant drips.
items.explanation: Fresh fluid under the truck points to a hydraulic, oil or coolant leak — find it before starting.

items.label: Lights & beacon
items.observation: Headlights, tail lights and the amber beacon all work.
items.explanation: The beacon and lights let other operators see you, especially at night and in dust.

items.label: Mirrors & cameras
items.observation: Mirrors clean and correctly adjusted, camera screen clear.
items.explanation: Mirrors and cameras cover the large blind spots around a haul truck.

items.label: Horn
items.observation: Horn sounds loud and clear.
items.explanation: The horn signals your intent: one blast before starting, two before moving forward, three before reversing.

items.label: Service & park brake test
items.observation: Truck holds on the park brake at full throttle test; service brake firm.
items.explanation: Brake tests must pass before every shift. Never operate with a failed brake test.

items.label: Seatbelt
items.observation: Buckle latches and the webbing is not frayed.
items.explanation: A seatbelt keeps you in the cab’s protective structure if the truck rolls.

items.label: Fire extinguisher
items.observation: Gauge in the green, pin and tamper seal in place.
items.explanation: The cab extinguisher is your first line of defence against a fire.

prestart.title: DT-12 · Night shift
prestart.brief: The previous operator reported “a noise at the back”. Inspect before accepting the truck.

items.label: Tyres & rims
items.observation: Deep cut in the left rear outer tyre sidewall, cords visible.
items.explanation: A sidewall cut with exposed cords can blow out under load. Tag out and call the tyre crew.

items.label: Fluid leaks
items.observation: Small damp patch of hydraulic oil under the hoist cylinder.
items.explanation: Report minor leaks so maintenance can fix them before they get worse.

items.label: Lights & beacon
items.observation: All lights and the beacon work.
items.explanation: The beacon and lights let other operators see you, especially at night and in dust.

items.label: Mirrors & cameras
items.observation: Mirrors adjusted; camera screen clear.
items.explanation: Mirrors and cameras cover the large blind spots around a haul truck.

items.label: Reversing alarm
items.observation: Alarm beeps when reverse is selected.
items.explanation: The reversing alarm warns people and vehicles behind the truck.

items.label: Horn
items.observation: Horn works.
items.explanation: The horn signals your intent before starting and moving.

items.label: Seatbelt
items.observation: Latches correctly.
items.explanation: A seatbelt keeps you in the cab’s protective structure if the truck rolls.

items.label: Fire extinguisher
items.observation: Gauge in the green, seal intact.
items.explanation: The cab extinguisher is your first line of defence against a fire.

prestart.title: DT-03 · After maintenance
prestart.brief: The truck just came back from the workshop. Do your full pre-start.

items.label: Tyres & rims
items.observation: Tyres good, wheel-nut indicators aligned.
items.explanation: Check for cuts, bulges, low pressure and loose wheel nuts on every wheel.

items.label: Lights & beacon
items.observation: Right tail light lens cracked but the light still works.
items.explanation: Report cosmetic damage so it is repaired; a working light with a cracked lens does not stop the shift.

items.label: Reversing alarm
items.observation: No sound when reverse is selected.
items.explanation: A silent reversing alarm puts people behind the truck at risk. Do not operate until fixed.

items.label: Mirrors & cameras
items.observation: Mirrors clean and adjusted.
items.explanation: Mirrors and cameras cover the large blind spots around a haul truck.

items.label: Service & park brake test
items.observation: Brake test passed.
items.explanation: Brake tests must pass before every shift.

items.label: Horn
items.observation: Horn works.
items.explanation: The horn signals your intent before starting and moving.

items.label: Seatbelt
items.observation: Webbing frayed along one edge.
items.explanation: A damaged seatbelt may fail in a rollover. The truck must not operate until it is replaced.

items.label: Fire extinguisher
items.observation: Bracket empty — extinguisher missing after maintenance.
items.explanation: Never operate without a charged extinguisher in the cab.
